chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Al-Hasan Al-Sayqal who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who does Zahir from his wife. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let him expiate.' I said, 'Supposing he copulates before he expiates?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He has exceeded a limit from the limits of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and let him seek forgiveness of Allah, and let him refrain (from his wife) until he has expiated.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man has intercourse with his wife before expiating Zahir?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that sexual intercourse prior to completing the Zahir expiation constitutes a distinct violation of divine limits (hadd), necessitating both seeking forgiveness (istighfar) and the completion of the prescribed expiation. This ruling highlights the juristic distinction between the act of Zahir itself and the subsequent intercourse, emphasizing that the man must refrain from his wife until the kaffarah is fully discharged, a nuance critical in Shia fiqh regarding the timing of expiation obligations. The emphasis on istighfar underscores the spiritual gravity of exceeding Allah's boundaries in marital relations.
